title: Brač Travel Guide: Beaches, Ferries & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan a trip to Brač, Croatia. Find the best areas to stay, driving routes to the Split ferry, beach information, and practical travel advice.
intro:
Brač is a large Dalmatian island suited for travelers looking for reliable beaches, active water sports, and traditional stone villages. It is less party-focused than neighboring Hvar, drawing a mix of families, windsurfers, and road-trippers exploring the Croatian coast. The island is best known for the Zlatni Rat beach in Bol and its historical limestone quarries.

The main visitor season runs from late May to early October, with the warmest sea temperatures peaking in July and August. Arriving usually involves a car ferry from the mainland port of Split to Supetar, or from Makarska to Sumartin, making it a highly accessible island for those driving down through Central Europe.

quickFacts.label: Best months
quickFacts.value: June to September for swimming and warm weather

quickFacts.label: Nearest airport
quickFacts.value: Brač Airport (BWK) is 15 km from Bol; Split Airport (SPU) requires a ferry

quickFacts.label: Main beach type
quickFacts.value: Mostly pebbles and fine gravel, with rare sandy bays

quickFacts.label: Price level
quickFacts.value: Slightly above the Croatian average, but lower than Hvar or Dubrovnik

quickFacts.label: Walkability
quickFacts.value: Old towns are pedestrian-only; a car is recommended for island exploration

areas.name: Bol
areas.parking: Paid public lots on the edge of town; central streets are restricted
areas.beach: 15-minute walk to the famous Zlatni Rat (fine pebbles)
areas.summary: Located on the southern coast, Bol is the island's most famous destination. It offers a long seaside promenade, numerous restaurants, and excellent windsurfing conditions.

areas.name: Supetar
areas.bestFor: Families and those wanting easy ferry access to Split
areas.parking: Plentiful paid parking areas near the ferry port and supermarkets
areas.beach: Several town beaches with pebbles, concrete terraces, and pine shade
areas.summary: As the main entry point to Brač, Supetar is a functional and lively town with excellent infrastructure. It provides easy mainland connections and a family-friendly coastal atmosphere.

areas.name: Sutivan
areas.bestFor: Cyclists and travelers seeking a quiet, low-traffic environment
areas.parking: Free and paid parking available on the village outskirts
areas.beach: Small pebble coves immediately accessible from the town centre
areas.summary: A peaceful village on the northwest coast known for its historic stone houses and strict summer traffic limits. It is well-connected by bike paths to nearby secluded bays.

areas.name: Postira
areas.bestFor: Couples and families looking for agricultural heritage and nearby sand
areas.parking: Designated public lots; narrow central streets have limited access
areas.beach: 3 km to Lovrečina Bay, one of the few sandy beaches on the island
areas.summary: A traditional fishing and farming village on the northern coast surrounded by olive groves. It serves as a quiet base with access to the sandy shores of Lovrečina.

whenToGo: The summer season from June to September is the most popular time to visit Brač, with August sea temperatures averaging around 25°C. July and August bring the highest prices, largest crowds, and full operation of all ferry routes, restaurants, and beach bars. May and October offer cooler weather and lower accommodation rates, but the sea is typically too cold for comfortable swimming and some seasonal businesses will be closed. From November to April, the island is very quiet, with many hotels shut for the winter and ferry schedules reduced.

faq.question: Is it worth visiting?
faq.answer: Brač is worth visiting for its reliable beaches, traditional stone architecture, and excellent windsurfing. It offers a more relaxed, family-oriented alternative to the nightlife-heavy island of Hvar.

faq.question: How many days should I spend on Brač?
faq.answer: Three to five days is optimal for a trip to Brač. This allows enough time to relax on Zlatni Rat, explore coastal villages like Supetar and Sutivan, and drive to the Vidova Gora viewpoint.

faq.question: Which is the best beach on the island?
faq.answer: Zlatni Rat in Bol is the most famous for its unique shape and smooth pebbles. For a sandy alternative, Lovrečina Bay near Postira is highly recommended, while Murvica offers quieter gravel shores.

faq.question: Do I need a car on Brač?
faq.answer: A car is highly beneficial for exploring the island's interior, remote coves, and varying towns. While local buses connect the main settlements, they run infrequently, making independent transport much more convenient.

faq.question: Where is the best place to park?
faq.answer: Most towns on Brač have designated, paid municipal parking lots on their outskirts. It is best to use these, as the historic centres feature narrow, often pedestrian-only stone streets that are difficult to navigate.

faq.question: Is Brač a good destination for families?
faq.answer: Yes, Brač is very family-friendly, offering calm waters, manageable towns, and plenty of self-catering apartments. Supetar and Postira are particularly popular with families due to their easy access to amenities and beaches.
